commit.message:
fix(teleprompt): raise a clear error when student predictors have no LM set (#10569)

* fix(teleprompt): raise a clear error when student predictors have no LM set

BetterTogether._prepare_student_and_teacher called
all_predictors_have_lms(student) and discarded the return value, so the
documented "all predictors must have language models assigned"
requirement was never enforced. Compilation only failed much later
inside launch_lms with AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no
attribute 'launch'.

That happens because Predict falls back to the global settings.lm only
at call time (predict.py), while launch_lms reads pred.lm directly with
no fallback, so a None predictor always crashes there.

Add assert_all_predictors_have_lms as the asserting counterpart of the
all_predictors_have_lms predicate and call it for the student, so the
failure happens up front and names the predictors that are missing an
LM plus the set_lm call that fixes them.

Fixes #10546

* fix(teleprompt): warn that set_lm overwrites existing predictor LMs

Review on #10569 noted that the error's advice, `student.set_lm(lm)`,
replaces the LM on every predictor, so a user with deliberately different
LMs per predictor would silently lose them while fixing the single missing
one.

Confirmed locally: Module.set_lm assigns to all named parameters, so a
per-predictor set_lm call is the non-destructive remedy.

State the overwrite explicitly in the message and pin it with a test.

* Remove outdated regression test comment

Removed regression test comment for issue 10546 from the test case.

Signed-off-by: Isaac Miller <17116851+isaacbmiller@users.noreply.github.com>
